question.text: Swasth Bharat Trust's immunisation program in a district achieves 90% coverage. State-wide trend data (without the Trust) shows 72% coverage in comparable districts. What is the deadweight percentage?

explanation.text: The Logic: Deadweight expressed as a percentage of the gross outcome = counterfactual outcome / gross outcome = 72 / 90 = 0.80 = 80%. That means 80% of the observed coverage would have happened anyway (via state trend); only 20% is net contribution. Equivalently 18 percentage-points of added coverage but 80% deadweight proportion. The Trap: 90% is the gross outcome. 72% is the absolute counterfactual coverage level. 18% is the absolute lift in percentage points. Deadweight as a proportion of gross = 72/90 = 80%. Cross-Exam Context: XV Research Analyst uses benchmark-adjusted alpha, analogous to deadweight-adjusted social alpha. XXIII expects the exact formula. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Ask the SE for the SOURCE of the deadweight benchmark (NFHS round, state health bulletin, etc.) and LOCK the citation in the working papers — deadweight disputes later will hinge on the source document being the one the district health officer accepts.
